request.name: Access and retain finite river water
request.function: Determine whether nearby observed river terrain provides accessible water, and if physically supported collect or use a finite amount for an existing material wet-comparison test.
request.conditions: Lin is at (25,15), beside observed river terrain beginning near x=26. The retained vine test lin-vine-test-79 previously stopped because actual reachable water was missing. No water container or usable water source has been established. Access must avoid unsafe entry into the river.
request.inputs: Observed river terrain; existing vine specimen item-78-lin-432 remains near (7.83,12.37). Suitable collection materials, transport requirements and method are unknown.
request.costs: Unknown; require actual finite source accounting, physical access, material and effort costs rather than supplied test water.
request.effects: Establish measured access limits and, only if feasible with real inputs, obtain finite usable contact water. Do not infer drinking safety or complete the vine test remotely.

Add versioned finite surface-water compartments only on actual river cells: initially 10 litres per square metre of wetted area, representing a declared 1 cm withdrawable surface layer, not measured actor knowledge or an unlimited river supply. No automatic replenishment in this minimal version. Persist cell volume, withdrawals, provenance and contamination-unknown status. Inspection reports geometric access and estimated available volume, not potability. If authoritative river geometry does not establish a water surface, report unresolved access without creating one.

Coordinate x=26 alone does not establish reach from (25,15). Inspection costs one round/0.2 energy and records actual bank/surface geometry and uncertainty. Declare model law: when holding water, lose 1 ml water and 0.1 g wall clay per round into an actual located spill containing clay sediment; at wall mass below 0.45 kg, collapse, spilling remaining water and retaining all clay as wet fragments. Use 10 ml per 0.1 material unit as the initial versioned contact-water dose, rounded upward to whole ml.
